correctness.rationale: On real ℓ²(Z) let d0=1, d±n=n, D=diag(dj), u±n=e^{−3n²/2}, u0 chosen to normalize, v=Du, κ=⟨v,u⟩. The nonpositive self-adjoint A0=−D+(v⊗v)/κ has a simple top 0 eigenvalue at u; compact resolvent plus a spectral gap imply e^{tA0}→u⊗u in norm. Antisymmetric q_n=(e_n−e_{−n})/√2 are A0 eigenvectors with eigenvalue −n. Add B=Σ δ_n q_n⊗q_n, δ_n=n e^{−2n²}, then A=A0+B remains real self-adjoint nonpositive compact-resolvent and e^{tA}=e^{tA0}+Σ e^{−nt}(e^{δ_nt}−1)q_n⊗q_n. The Dyson expansion bounds a_n(t)=⟨e^{tA0}e_n,e_−n⟩ by n²e^{−3n²}(e^{2t}−1), using b=||v||²/κ<2. The correction is −(1/2)e^{−nt}(e^{δ_nt}−1), at most −(nt/2)e^{−2n²−nt}. For every REAL t>0 and integer n≥ceil(t+3), e^{n²−nt}≥e^{3n}>4ne^{2t}, giving strict negative off-diagonal entry. Duhamel positivity and e^{tA0}→u⊗u yield an eventual c_xu lower bound on each positive nonzero orbit; the antisymmetric perturbation has sup_t h_n(t)/u_n≤e^{−n²/2}/[e(1−e^{−2n²})]→0 and finitely many remaining n decay in time. Identity at t=0 is positive. Source verify.py was inspected and independent rational-time inequality checks corroborated estimates; none substitutes for the all-real-time proof.

originality.rationale: Dobrick's exact self-adjoint compact-resolvent generator and its individual eventual strong positivity are expressly PRIOR; available first-version abstract says operators fail positivity at arbitrarily large times without asserting an all-time obstruction. The submitted package attributes a stronger inspected-in-package theorem/proposition comparison only at certain large integer times, but the primary complete text could not be independently checked here. The submitted work's new analytic comparison supplies simultaneous negativity for EVERY t>0 and quantitative n≥ceil(t+3). The general nowhere-positive phenomenon in Daners–Glück–Kennedy 2016 is known on C(K), with different generators; no demonstrated theorem transfers all structural properties and the explicit cutoff to this particular Hilbert-lattice operator. Another Resultary spectral-level barrier treats limited spectral-level systems, not shown to imply this infinitely spectral diagonal-plus-rank-one case. Full primary Dobrick paper inaccessible in this execution, so unverified theorem/appendix or newer revision remains a significant but not independently decisive originality risk.
